summary: Built and recorded the ordered candidate list before screening (fleet-shape axes only; Squidex removed on the T006 never-recycle graveyard). Screened five real MIT Angular apps in that fixed order with exactly the three checks, manifests/registry/published-bytes only. All five passed LICENSE-at-pin (named holders, blob sha1 recomputed against the pinned tree) and UNUSED; all five failed BOUNDARY on distinct no-successor ViewEngine libraries in active module-scope use. No candidate committed, no acquisition, no baseline/migration/trial. tsc and lint pass; the ingest-presence verify fails by design.
open_questions: No candidate passed the three-check screen, so nothing was committed or acquired. Per-candidate: (1) cyclos4-ui@2.0.0 c1e902bd, MIT 'Copyright (c) 2017 Cyclos' licenseSha256 0f593612..., unused, FAILS on ngx-gallery-9@1.0.6 (sole dist-tag, ViewEngine metadata.json, zero Ivy markers in fesm2015) at shared.module.ts:115; no family successor (ngx-gallery dead 5.10.0, @kolkov/ngx-gallery dead at Angular 13). (2) ngx-starter-kit@v3.3.0 50d7cfc2, MIT 'Sumanth Chinthagunta' 30b59add..., unused, FAILS on @xmlking/ngx-knob@1.1.1 at experiments.module.ts:5, plus ngx-perfect-scrollbar@10.1.1 and @ngxs-labs/immer-adapter@3.0.5. (3) eShopOnContainers@netcore2.2 a387f210, MIT '.NET Foundation' baebca03..., unused, FAILS on @angular/http (newest line 7.2.16, no Angular 8+ line) at shared.module.ts:5; preboot is ViewEngine but declared-and-never-imported so it does not fail. (4) tabby@v1.0.160 881d5d59, MIT 'Eugene Pankov' 14922f6f..., unused, FAILS on ngx-sortablejs@11.1.0 and ngx-perfect-scrollbar at tabby-core/src/index.ts:8 and :6. (5) coreui-free-angular-admin-template@v2.9.6 6cd7a011, MIT 'creativeLabs Lukasz Holeczek' 31bf25a5..., unused, FAILS on ngx-perfect-scrollbar at app.module.ts:6.

DECISION NEEDED on candidate 3: is @angular/http a boundary failure? It satisfies the declared condition literally (newest published line 7.2.16 is ViewEngine-era, no Angular 8+ line exists, active at module scope, carrying it requires editing application source at the import sites). I ruled FAIL because the counter-reading -- that a first-party removal with a documented @angular/common/http successor is adapter work rather than a boundary -- rests on what the adapter can do, which is the forbidden screening axis; and because @angular/http appears zero times across the ingest evidence of all four counted Angular verticals, so no green vertical has demonstrated the engine carrying it. If the Judge prefers the counter-reading, eShopOnContainers netcore2.2 is the candidate to re-open and it would then be committable.

DECISION NEEDED on how to proceed: (a) extend the ordered list, appending only to the bottom so already-screened candidates are never leapfrogged -- note the MIT-and-unused Angular population left after the licence and graveyard refusals in section 2 is genuinely thin; (b) re-open candidate 3 per the ruling above; or (c) take the tranche-two ngcc-bearing Angular 12/13 multi-hop cell, which T022 already declared as a commitment and which is the mechanism that would consume all five offending libraries -- its stated cost (it invalidates every Angular 16 cell reading in the record) is unchanged.

FINDING for the Judge, not a request: the boundary knocked out five of five independently-selected candidates across Angular 6/9/10/12 and four build generations, with ngx-perfect-scrollbar alone reaching three of them. The published non-claim ('not-certified: declared unsupported, not tested-and-failed-once') may now understate the condition's prevalence, and any app that eventually clears this gate is by construction one whose whole third-party Angular surface is still maintained -- a narrower population than the webpack-era enterprise fleet the goal targets.
